Disclosure control settings for small populations

mimic_config.Rd

Creates the configuration object used by profile_data(), mimic(), real_run() and inspect(). The defaults are deliberately stricter than in tools designed for large countries: in a small population with many settlements of a few hundred people, a cell of 3 is often a known household.

Usage

mimic_config(
  min_count = 5,
  dominance = list(n = 2, k = 0.85),
  p_percent = 0.1,
  quasi_ids = character(),
  geo_vars = character(),
  id_vars = character(),
  text_vars = character(),
  date_unit = c("month", "year"),
  tail_coding = c(0.01, 0.99),
  round_base = 5,
  signif_digits = 2,
  min_persons = 100,
  min_df = 10,
  other_label = "Other",
  require_description = FALSE
)

Arguments

min_count

Smallest number of persons allowed behind any category, cell or bin. Must be at least 3.

dominance

List with n (number of largest contributors) and k (maximum share they may hold) for the (n, k) dominance rule.

p_percent

Threshold for the p % rule, as a proportion.

quasi_ids

Character vector of quasi-identifiers (for example age, sex, settlement). Rare combinations are reported by profile_data().

geo_vars

Character vector of geographical variables. Small units are merged according to min_count.

id_vars

Character vector of identifier variables. Only their type and format are stored, never values. Key variables are always treated as identifiers.

text_vars

Character vector of free-text variables. Only an approximate length is stored. Character columns with many unique long values are also detected automatically.

date_unit

Granularity for dates: "month" or "year".

tail_coding

Lower and upper quantile used for bottom and top coding.

round_base

Counts are rounded to a multiple of this number.

signif_digits

Number of significant digits kept in summary values and bin edges.

min_persons

Smallest number of persons for which synthesis above level 2 is considered safe.

min_df

Smallest residual degrees of freedom accepted for a model in inspect().

other_label

Label used for merged categories.

require_description

TRUE makes inspect() send back every output file that has no description from describe_output().

Value

An object of class mimic_config.

Why these defaults

  • min_count = 5 is the floor used by most national statistical offices. Raise it to 10 for health data or very small settlements.

  • The tail quantiles in tail_coding are never allowed to fall on fewer than min_count people. With 40 rows, the 1 % quantile is one person's value, so profile_data() uses max(tail_coding[1], min_count / n).

  • The dominance rule (n = 2, k = 0.85) and the p % rule follow the Eurostat guidelines for output checking: no two contributors may make up 85 % of a sum, and no contributor may be estimated within 10 % by the second largest.

Examples

cfg <- mimic_config(
  min_count = 10,
  quasi_ids = c("birth_date", "sex", "settlement"),
  geo_vars = "settlement"
)
cfg
#> <mimic_config>
#> • min_count: 10
#> • dominance: (n = 2, k = 0.85); p % rule: 0.1
#> • tail coding: 0.01 / 0.99; date unit: month
#> • rounding: counts to 5, values to 2 significant digits
#> • quasi-identifiers: birth_date, sex, settlement
#> • geographical: settlement
#> • identifiers: (none)
#> • free text: (none)
#> • min persons for synthesis: 100; min model df: 10
#> • merged category label: "Other"
#> • descriptions of output: optional
